  - paragraph: Discover why opposite angles formed by intersecting lines are equal.

    - text: ⓘ Drag either line (p or q), or use Rotate, to explore.
    - article:
      - heading "💡 Why it works" [level=2]
      - paragraph: When two lines intersect, vertical angles have their sides extended in opposite directions.
      - paragraph: They are formed by the same pair of lines, so they are always equal.
      - img
      - paragraph: Adjacent angles form a linear pair and always sum to 180°.
    - article:
      - heading "▣ Worked Example" [level=2]
      - paragraph: If ∠1 = 68°, find all other angles.
      - list:
        - listitem: ∠1 and ∠3 are vertically opposite. So, ∠3 = 68°.
        - listitem: ∠1 and ∠2 form a linear pair. ∠2 = 180° − 68° = 112°.
        - listitem: ∠2 and ∠4 are vertically opposite. So, ∠4 = 112°.
      - text: ∠1 68°
      - img
      - text: ∠2 112°
      - img
      - text: ∠3 68°
      - img
      - text: ∠4 112°
      - img
    - article:
      - heading "△ Common Misconception" [level=2]
      - paragraph: Vertical angles are opposite, not adjacent.
      - img
      - text: "Correct: ∠1 and ∠3 are vertical."
      - img
      - text: "Incorrect: ∠1 and ∠2 are adjacent."
    - heading "🏆 Challenge" [level=2]
    - paragraph: Drag line q to make ∠1 an obtuse angle of 125°. Then predict all four angles.
    - strong: Target ∠1 = 125°
